sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Styled accordion parts
sections.what: Defines the four parts of an accordion: the outer container, each item with a bottom border, the clickable heading with an arrow, and the hidden content with an open and close animation. Together these let a page show expandable sections that all look the same.
sections.why: Keeps the Radix behavior from the library and adds only the app's look, so the page does not repeat styling.
sections.watch_out: The arrow rotation and the animation rely on state names that the Radix library sets, so renaming the states breaks them.

summary: A set of styled, expandable panels where clicking a heading opens or closes its content.
purpose: Lets a page show long content in collapsible sections, such as a list of questions and answers.
why: Likely reason: this is a styled wrapper so every accordion in the app looks the same. Reason not stated in the code.
how: Step 1: Loads the accordion behavior from the Radix library and the arrow icon. Step 2: Wraps the outer container and each item, giving each item a bottom border. Step 3: Wraps the clickable heading, adding padding, bold text and an arrow that turns when the panel is open. Step 4: Wraps the hidden content, adding open and close animation and padding. Step 5: Makes the four parts available to other files.
inputs: Text or other content placed inside each part, plus any extra style classes the page passes in.
outputs: Expandable sections on screen. Clicking a heading toggles its section open or closed.
risks: The open and close animation depends on animation rules defined elsewhere in the project. Without them, panels still open but without motion.
debug: If panels do not open, check that the page uses the items and triggers from this file and that the Radix accordion package is installed. If the animation is missing, check the project's Tailwind configuration for the accordion animation names. If the arrow does not turn, check the open-state styling on the trigger.
